💡 Women are 28% of the STEM workforce, 19% of all CS majors, and 18% of all CIOs & CTOs at top tech firms. Help change that at Superposition V. Superposition V, the Bay Area’s largest all-female & non-binary hackathon for high school and college students, is going global from April 9-11! We’ve planned 3 immersive days of various workshops, panels, networking events, learning opportunities, and projects -- all for free. No coding experience is necessary -- 77% of our past hackathon attendees were first-time hackers and 35% were first-time programmers -- and mentors will be available throughout the hackathon. We have over $4,500+ in prizes, from iPads to $250 gaming sets, and all attendees will also be entered in various raffles! Register at http://bit.ly/sp5_JiminH to join us in #BreakingBoundaries ! Feel free to reach out if you have any questions! Learn more at www.superposition.tech Follow us on Instagram at @superpositionfc to keep up with more updates! #networking #womeninstemm #hackathon #coding #empowerwomen #tech #students #opportunities ...more

Calling all Korean and Korean American women in my network! 💄 Bay Area conversations are full of tech and AI, but it can be surprisingly hard to find spaces to talk about K-beauty from a business and brand-building perspective. So we decided to create one. I’m excited to share that BayJoyce is hosting our first K-Beauty Table on Friday, August 21 in San Francisco, bringing together founders and marketing leaders who are actively shaping the Korean beauty and lifestyle landscape in the U.S. We’ll be joined by: ✨ Sungbin An, Founder & CEO of Skyne Beauty and ex-Meta ✨ Kipeum Lee, Co-founder & COO of Saelo and ex-Airbnb ✨ Jenny Seo, Marketing Strategist at Yami and ex-Samyang Foods, who is flying in from LA for the event Together, we’ll explore both sides of the journey: *Building the Brand from 0 to 1 How founders transition from corporate careers, identify market gaps, and create differentiated K-beauty businesses for U.S. consumers. *Selling & Scaling in the U.S. How brands can navigate consumer trends, develop viral content and influencer strategies, and translate attention into e-commerce growth. This event is for Korean and Korean American women in the Bay Area who are interested in K-beauty, entrepreneurship, marketing, or simply meeting others who share that curiosity. 📅 Friday, August 21, 6:00 to 9:00 PM 📍 San Francisco 🗣️ All sessions will be in English 🎟️ Event fee: $15 🎁 The first 20 attendees to check in will also receive a goodie bag featuring over $60 worth of K-beauty products, generously supported by SOOO, bee:nuvo, Yami, and Meebak. RSVP here: https://luma.com/dd2hikyh Hope to see many of you there!

AI coding tools deliver immense value but deploying them at scale has led to a major challenge: exponentially growing costs. Databricks co-founder and VP of Engineering at Databricks, Patrick Wendell , outlines what strategies the Databricks team uses to manage AI coding costs at scale. Across Databricks and other early AI adopters, four techniques are emerging as a consistent playbook for bringing costs down: - Adopting more efficient and OSS models - Dynamic model routing - Empowering individuals and teams to make better consumption decisions - Optimizing context management See the full playbook https://lnkd.in/gDcMTbjK

It’s a big day for Oura in San Francisco. I’ve lived in the Bay Area for more than 20 years, and there’s nowhere else I’d rather call home. The energy, talent, and creativity of this city are unmatched and I’m proud to help kick off a new chapter for Oura here. Owning our SF office is a reflection of our confidence in the future we’re building—as a company, a category leader, and a team. Oura was founded in Finland over a decade ago, and those roots remain strong. Much of our global team continues to build and operate in Finland, and today San Francisco has become the center of gravity for our leadership team as well as a growing cohort of cross-functional talent. 500 Pine gives us a lasting home for Oura’s next era of growth, innovation, and leadership. I’m excited for what’s ahead and grateful to everyone who helped make this milestone possible.
